Recommendations ### Redis - Bind Redis to localhost or a private management network only. - Require authentication using `requirepass` or ACLs. - Firewall port `6379` from untrusted networks. - Disable dangerous commands where appropriate. - Review Redis data for unauthorized modification. ### Apache / CGI / Shellshock - Patch Bash and remove vulnerable CGI exposure. - Disable CGI if not required. - Remove or restrict `/victim.cgi`. - Upgrade Apache from `2.4.10` to a supported patched version. - Review web server logs for Shellshock-style payloads. - Ensure CGI scripts do not pass attacker-controlled environment variables to vulnerable interpreters. ### Flask/Werkzeug Application - Implement server-side authorization checks for every `/profile/` request. - Ensure users can only access their own records unless explicitly authorized. - Avoid exposing secrets in profile responses. - Disable debug features and Werkzeug console in production. - Add security headers: - `X-Frame-Options` or CSP `frame-ancestors` - `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` - Appropriate `Content-Security-Policy` ### SSH - Remove deprecated `ssh-rsa` host-key algorithm support if not required. - Prefer modern algorithms such as ED25519 and ECDSA. - Enforce key-based authentication where possible. - Monitor for password-authentication attempts. ### General - Restrict unnecessary exposed services. - Remove default Apache pages and files. - Harden firewall rules to expose only required services. - Centralize logging and monitor for: - Redis unauthenticated access - CGI Shellshock payloads - Unexpected outbound reverse connections - Unauthorized profile enumeration patterns --- ## Final Assessment Conclusion The lab host exposes several high-impact weaknesses. The most severe issue is confirmed unauthenticated remote command execution through Shellshock on the Apache CGI service at `192.168.185.3:8080`. Redis on `192.168.185.3:6379` is also critically exposed, allowing unauthenticated read and write operations. The Werkzeug application on `192.168.185.3:5000` contains a validated IDOR vulnerability exposing multiple user records, including admin-associated secret data. A controlled initial foothold was established through Shellshock, read-only post-exploitation enumeration was performed, and the approved bounded lateral-movement and privilege-escalation proof succeeded without exposing credentials. Cleanup was confirmed where tooling supported confirmation, and no persistence or destructive actions were attempted.
